title: Opera introduces a new web standard to let users deploy AI locally in their browser
slides: Can Opera run AI without the cloud?
Opera proposes a new web standard for local AI
It executes models directly inside the browser
Sites may soon offload AI work to your device
Check if your browser supports local inference
thread_text:
1. Your browser could run AI

Opera just proposed a new web standard that lets sites execute AI models directly inside your browser, no cloud required.

2. No cloud, no delay

Local inference means your device handles the computation, so responses can be faster and your data never leaves your machine.

3. A new web standard

Opera's proposal would let any website offload AI work to your device, turning your browser into a personal AI engine.

4. Sites will offload work

Soon, instead of sending every prompt to a server, websites may ask your device to run the model, cutting costs and latency.

5. Does your browser do this?

Open your browser's settings and search for 'local inference' or 'on-device AI'. If it's missing, you're not ready yet.

instagram.caption:
Your browser might soon run AI models itself, without sending anything to a server.

Opera proposed a new web standard that lets websites execute AI models directly on your device instead of in the cloud. It's called local inference, and it means the computation happens on your machine.

That could cut latency and keep your data from leaving your computer. Sites would offload the work to you rather than paying for servers. 🔒

If you publish content or build tools, this changes what you can ship: AI features that run on the reader's device, no API bills attached. ⚡

Open your browser settings and search "local inference." If it's missing, you're not there yet. Does yours have it? 🧐
